The LisaGB prior by parameter group: f₀, ḟ, A · polarization · sky · response span

The LisaGB prior: f₀, ḟ and A

(log₁₀ f₀, log₁₀ ḟ, log₁₀ A) is one Gaussian, fitted to the double white dwarfs of a galaxy catalogue. The catalogue prior (k = 0) draws a window centre from its f₀ marginal (sample_f) and 4 sources from the Gaussian inside the window. This page shows that joint prior, which of its sources the data see, and what the flow is given. The cut slider's k > 0 centres windows by sample_window at LisaGB(visible_snr=k), about the f₀ of a source at SNR ≥ k; the sources inside stay catalogue draws. Training uses k = 7, the slider's default. Measured on 8,192 windows per band (32,768 sources), 4,096 per cut. Built 2026-10-30 from data/ (commit dc78e7c, src dirty).

Band Cut

The joint prior, as training draws it

The corner of the three log parameters. The diagonal holds each one's density; the cells below it hold each pair's, smoothed by a one-cell Gaussian on a 64 × 64 grid, filled more opaque where denser and outlined where it holds 39% and 86% of the sources (1σ and 2σ in 2-D). The dashed contours are the catalogue's Gaussian truncated to the band and to the ḟ ceiling, from a million numpy draws: where they meet the drawn ones, training follows the catalogue. The orange dots are the sources at SNR ≥ 7, with their own density on the diagonal; the orange line in (f₀, A) is the amplitude a source needs for SNR 7, averaged over sky and orientation: 7 · amplitude_unit / √⟨κ²⟩, with κ the SNR of one amplitude unit; at a cut, the green line is the same amplitude at SNR k.

Which windows hold a source the data see?

Top: where window centres fall, in 24 log bins: at k = 0 the catalogue's f₀ marginal, so most windows sit low; at a cut, sample_window's. Bottom: per centre bin, the share of windows holding at least k sources at SNR ≥ 7, and (dashed) the share of single sources. A window is 4 response bands wide, so its centre and its sources' f₀ agree to a few percent.

What the flow is given

Per source in f₀ order, what the flow learns: z = (x − μ) / σ of each chart coordinate in the prior's frame (chart.prior_moments), the frame the network starts from before the data shift it, and its best answer where the data see nothing. The flow transports its N(0, 1) base (dashed) to z. z± is the helicity coordinate, asinh(A/unit · (1 ∓ sin ι)²/4) times its phase; hover for each z's std and its share beyond the axis.

What the cut does

At cut k, sample_window draws M = 64 log-uniform window-centre candidates, each a source alone at the centre with one prior sky and orientation, and resamples them by p(f₀) · P(SNR ≥ k | f₀, sky, orientation), the latter Φ(−cut) with cut where SNR = k falls in log₁₀ A given f₀, in stds. The window's sources stay catalogue draws, so the cut moves windows, not sources. Top: source SNR, sin ι and galactic latitude, against the catalogue draws (dashed). Bottom, over the first 1,024 windows: per f₀ bin, P(SNR ≥ k) from the candidates' Φ(−cut) (solid) and the catalogue draws' share (dashed); per window-centre bin, the share of the M candidates the resample keeps (ESS / M). The table holds every cut of the band; click a row to show it.

What this means

  • The draws follow the catalogue. The drawn means sit within 0.00094 (narrow-B) and 0.0029 (full-B) stds of the catalogue Gaussian truncated to the band, and the contours overlap. 98.0% of the catalogue lies in narrow-B, below 1.26 mHz.
  • Almost every source is invisible. 0.05% of narrow-B sources and 0.84% of full-B ones reach SNR 7; 99.80% and 98.47% of windows hold none, so for them the flow's best answer is the prior. The conditional mean A reaches the SNR-7 amplitude from 1.99 mHz.
  • The visible sources sit at the top of the band, where the catalogue's windows rarely go. Half the full-B windows hold a visible source only from about 1.63 mHz, while the upper half of the band in log f₀ gets 3.08% of the windows: hence training's k = 7 window prior.
  • ḟ matters only in full-B. 0.07% of full-B sources drift by more than a bin over the observation (narrow-B 0%); every response still fits: the widest spans 112 of 128 bins (narrow-B 32 of 32).
  • The cut moves windows to where sources are visible; it does not make them visible. At SNR ≥ 7, 80.2% of full-B windows hold a source that loud (catalogue 1.53%), narrow-B 8.1% (catalogue 0.20%). Full-B median ESS / M falls from 0.24 at SNR ≥ 1 to 0.18 at SNR ≥ 20 (5% quantile 0.18 to 0.12). The candidates' prior mass at SNR ≥ 7 is 0.69% against the uncut draws' 0.84% (full-B), and narrow-B 0.036% against 0.049%.
  • What the flow is given is a unit normal, at every cut. At SNR ≥ 7 (full-B) all eight z have std 0.985 to 1.01, and 1.5e-03% of z± lies beyond ±5 (a unit normal: 6e-5%). The cut moves the median source from 10-1.88 to 100.65 amplitude units, and the prior's frame follows it.
